questions.question: What is the first step of the scientific method?
questions.correctAnswer: Ask a question or make an observation
questions.explanation: Science starts with a question or observation about the world.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: curiosity starts every experiment.

questions.question: What is the main job of the immune system?
distractors: sends signals and controls the body
brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: White blood cells patrol the body, attack invaders, and remember germs they have beaten before.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each body system has one big job.

questions.question: What is a food chain?
questions.correctAnswer: a series showing who eats whom in an ecosystem
distractors: an animal that is hunted for food
an organism that eats other organisms for energy
many connected food chains in an ecosystem
questions.explanation: food chain: a series showing who eats whom in an ecosystem. (a single path of energy flow)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: What is the main job of the digestive system?
distractors: brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Food is broken down step by step - chewing, stomach acid, and enzymes - until nutrients are small enough to pass into the blood.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each body system has one big job.

questions.question: What is the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release energy from food, so they are called the powerhouse.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: mighty mitochondria make energy.

questions.question: What is an allele?
distractors: a chart that predicts the possible offspring of a cross
a trait that shows up even if only one copy is inherited
a characteristic that can be passed from parent to offspring
questions.explanation: allele: one version of a gene. (for example, the allele for brown eyes)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genetics words build on each other, learn them in order.

questions.question: Why do cells divide?
questions.correctAnswer: For growth and to repair damaged tissue
questions.explanation: Cell division lets organisms grow and replaces old or damaged cells.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: division is how bodies grow and heal.

questions.question: What is the correct order from smallest to largest?
questions.explanation: Cells group into tissues, tissues form organs, and organs work together in systems.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: think of it like bricks, walls, rooms, house.

questions.question: What do decomposers do in an ecosystem?
questions.correctAnswer: Break down dead organisms and return nutrients to the soil
questions.explanation: Decomposers like fungi and bacteria recycle nutrients from dead things.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: decomposers are nature's recyclers.

questions.question: Which organelle gives a plant cell shape and protection?
questions.explanation: The stiff cell wall wraps the plant cell like a box, holding its shape and shielding it from damage.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: match the job to the worker.

questions.question: What is a producer?
questions.correctAnswer: an organism that makes its own food, like a plant
distractors: a trait that helps an organism survive in its environment
a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is not affected
a relationship where both organisms benefit
questions.explanation: producer: an organism that makes its own food, like a plant. (the base of a food chain)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: What is a genotype?
questions.correctAnswer: the genes an organism has for a trait
distractors: a change in the DNA sequence
passing traits from parents to offspring
a trait that shows up even if only one copy is inherited
questions.explanation: genotype: the genes an organism has for a trait. (the genetic code, like Bb)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genetics words build on each other, learn them in order.

questions.question: In an experiment, what is the independent variable?
questions.correctAnswer: The thing the scientist changes on purpose
questions.explanation: The independent variable is what the scientist changes to test its effect.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: independent means the scientist controls it.

questions.question: What is a commensalism?
questions.correctAnswer: a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is not affected
distractors: a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is harmed
a relationship where both organisms benefit
the place where an organism lives
questions.explanation: commensalism: a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is not affected. (like barnacles on a whale)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: What is a decomposer?
questions.correctAnswer: an organism that breaks down dead material
distractors: a relationship where both organisms benefit
an animal that hunts other animals for food
a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is harmed
questions.explanation: decomposer: an organism that breaks down dead material. (like fungi and bacteria)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: Which organ is a main part of the muscular system?
questions.explanation: Muscles are the key organs of the muscular system: they pull on bones to move the body.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pair each system with its star organ.

questions.question: What is a Punnett square?
questions.correctAnswer: a chart that predicts the possible offspring of a cross
distractors: a structure made of DNA that carries many genes
a section of DNA that codes for one trait
the molecule that carries genetic instructions
questions.explanation: Punnett square: a chart that predicts the possible offspring of a cross. (a tool for predicting traits)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genetics words build on each other, learn them in order.

questions.question: Where does photosynthesis happen in a plant cell?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts hold chlorophyll, the green pigment that captures sunlight.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: chloroplasts are the solar panels of the cell.

questions.question: What is the function of the cytoplasm?
questions.correctAnswer: the jelly-like fluid where most cell activities happen
distractors: gives a plant cell shape and protection
questions.explanation: The cytoplasm is the jelly-like fluid that fills the cell; organelles float in it and most chemical reactions happen there.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each organelle has one main job to remember.

questions.question: Which of these is an omnivore?
questions.explanation: A bear eats both plants and animals, so it is an omnivore.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: omni means all: omnivores eat everything.

questions.question: What is a predator?
questions.correctAnswer: an animal that hunts other animals for food
distractors: the place where an organism lives
an organism that breaks down dead material
a relationship where both organisms benefit
questions.explanation: predator: an animal that hunts other animals for food. (like a lion)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: What is the function of the nucleus?
questions.correctAnswer: controls the cell and holds the DNA
distractors: controls what enters and leaves the cell
the jelly-like fluid where most cell activities happen
releases energy from food through cellular respiration
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the DNA instructions and tells the cell what to do, like a brain giving orders to the body.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each organelle has one main job to remember.

questions.question: What is a prey?
questions.correctAnswer: an animal that is hunted for food
distractors: a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is not affected
many connected food chains in an ecosystem
an organism that breaks down dead material
questions.explanation: prey: an animal that is hunted for food. (like a rabbit)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: What is the function of the Golgi apparatus?
questions.explanation: Proteins arrive at the Golgi, get folded and labeled, then are shipped out in tiny sacs to where they are needed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each organelle has one main job to remember.

questions.question: What is the control center of the cell?
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds DNA and directs cell activities.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the nucleus is the boss of the cell.

questions.question: What is a trait?
questions.correctAnswer: a characteristic that can be passed from parent to offspring
distractors: the genes an organism has for a trait
a structure made of DNA that carries many genes
questions.explanation: trait: a characteristic that can be passed from parent to offspring. (like eye color or hair type)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genetics words build on each other, learn them in order.

questions.question: What is the main job of the skeletal system?
questions.correctAnswer: supports the body and protects organs
distractors: moves blood, oxygen, and nutrients around the body
sends signals and controls the body
questions.explanation: Bones hold the body upright, give muscles something to pull on, and shield soft organs like the brain and heart.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each body system has one big job.

questions.question: Which organelle captures sunlight for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll inside the chloroplast traps sunlight, and that light energy powers the making of sugar.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: match the job to the worker.

questions.question: In a food chain, what happens to energy as it moves up?
questions.correctAnswer: Most of it is lost at each step
questions.explanation: Only about 10 percent of energy passes to the next level; the rest is used or lost as heat.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: energy shrinks as it climbs the food chain.

questions.question: What is the main job of the nervous system?
questions.correctAnswer: sends signals and controls the body
distractors: supports the body and protects organs
questions.explanation: Nerves carry fast electrical signals from the brain to the body and back, so the body can react in a split second.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each body system has one big job.

questions.question: Which organelle makes proteins?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes read instructions and build proteins.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ribosomes build the proteins.

questions.question: What is DNA?
questions.correctAnswer: the molecule that carries genetic instructions
distractors: a section of DNA that codes for one trait
the genes an organism has for a trait
a characteristic that can be passed from parent to offspring
questions.explanation: DNA: the molecule that carries genetic instructions. (deoxyribonucleic acid)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genetics words build on each other, learn them in order.

questions.question: What is a parasitism?
questions.correctAnswer: a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is harmed
distractors: an organism that breaks down dead material
an animal that hunts other animals for food
an organism that makes its own food, like a plant
questions.explanation: parasitism: a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is harmed. (like a tick on a dog)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: What is a phenotype?
questions.correctAnswer: the visible trait an organism shows
distractors: a characteristic that can be passed from parent to offspring
a change in the DNA sequence
the genes an organism has for a trait
questions.explanation: phenotype: the visible trait an organism shows. (what you can actually see)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genetics words build on each other, learn them in order.

questions.question: Which process do plants use to make food from sunlight?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make glucose and oxygen.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: photo means light, synthesis means building.

questions.question: Which body system is at work here? Your muscles help you lift a backpack.
questions.explanation: Lifting a backpack uses your muscles, so it is the job of the muscular system.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: link the action to the system.

questions.question: What is a food web?
questions.correctAnswer: many connected food chains in an ecosystem
distractors: the place where an organism lives
a relationship where both organisms benefit
an animal that hunts other animals for food
questions.explanation: food web: many connected food chains in an ecosystem. (a map of feeding relationships)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: Which organ is a main part of the respiratory system?
questions.explanation: The lungs are the key organs of the respiratory system: air flows in, oxygen passes into the blood, and carbon dioxide passes out.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pair each system with its star organ.

questions.question: What is the main function of a leaf?
questions.explanation: Leaves hold chloroplasts that capture sunlight for photosynthesis.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: leaves are the kitchens of the plant.

questions.question: What is the job of red blood cells?
questions.correctAnswer: To carry oxygen around the body
questions.explanation: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: red blood cells are oxygen delivery trucks.

questions.question: What is an adaptation?
questions.correctAnswer: a trait that helps an organism survive in its environment
distractors: a series showing who eats whom in an ecosystem
an organism that makes its own food, like a plant
a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is harmed
questions.explanation: adaptation: a trait that helps an organism survive in its environment. (like thick fur in cold places)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: What is the function of the vacuole?
distractors: the jelly-like fluid where most cell activities happen
controls what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explanation: The large vacuole in a plant cell holds water and nutrients, and when it is full it pushes against the cell wall and keeps the plant firm.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each organelle has one main job to remember.

questions.question: What is the function of the cell membrane?
questions.correctAnswer: controls what enters and leaves the cell
distractors: controls the cell and holds the DNA
gives a plant cell shape and protection
questions.explanation: The thin membrane lets food and oxygen in and keeps harmful things out, like a gate with a guard.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each organelle has one main job to remember.

questions.question: What is a habitat?
questions.correctAnswer: the place where an organism lives
distractors: a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is harmed
an organism that eats other organisms for energy
a series showing who eats whom in an ecosystem
questions.explanation: habitat: the place where an organism lives. (it provides food, water, and shelter)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood through the body?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through the circulatory system.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the heart never stops pumping.

questions.question: What is a control group in an experiment?
questions.correctAnswer: A group that is not changed, used for comparison
distractors: The group with the most variables
The group that writes the report
questions.explanation: The control group gives a baseline to compare against the tested group.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a control is the comparison group.

questions.question: What does a Punnett square show?
questions.explanation: A Punnett square predicts the possible gene combinations of children.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Punnett squares predict the odds, not the exact child.

questions.question: If both parents have the genotype Bb for brown eyes (B is dominant), what is the chance of a child with blue eyes (bb)?
questions.explanation: The Punnett square gives BB, Bb, Bb, bb: one out of four, or 25 percent, is bb.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: one box out of four is bb.

questions.question: What is the main job of the respiratory system?
questions.correctAnswer: brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide
distractors: moves blood, oxygen, and nutrients around the body
supports the body and protects organs
questions.explanation: Air travels down the windpipe into the lungs, where oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each body system has one big job.

questions.question: What is natural selection?
questions.correctAnswer: Organisms with helpful traits survive and pass them on
distractors: Organisms choose which traits to have
All organisms change in the same way
Traits are picked at random by scientists
questions.explanation: Natural selection is survival of the best-adapted: helpful traits spread over generations.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: nature keeps the traits that work.

questions.question: Which organ is a main part of the digestive system?
questions.explanation: The stomach churns food and mixes it with acid, starting the breakdown of proteins.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pair each system with its star organ.

questions.question: What is homeostasis?
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping the inside of the body stable
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the body keeping conditions like temperature steady inside.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: homeo means same, stasis means staying.

questions.question: What is a chromosome?
questions.correctAnswer: a structure made of DNA that carries many genes
distractors: passing traits from parents to offspring
a change in the DNA sequence
a chart that predicts the possible offspring of a cross
questions.explanation: chromosome: a structure made of DNA that carries many genes. (found in the nucleus)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genetics words build on each other, learn them in order.

questions.question: What is the function of the mitochondria?
questions.correctAnswer: releases energy from food through cellular respiration
distractors: the jelly-like fluid where most cell activities happen
gives a plant cell shape and protection
questions.explanation: Mitochondria break down glucose with oxygen, releasing the energy (ATP) the cell uses to do its work.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each organelle has one main job to remember.

questions.question: What do plant cells have that animal cells do not?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a stiff cell wall and chloroplasts for photosynthesis; animal cells do not.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plants need walls and sunlight catchers, animals do not.

questions.question: Which organelle controls what enters and leaves the cell?
questions.explanation: The membrane is a selective barrier: it lets nutrients and oxygen in and waste out.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: match the job to the worker.

questions.question: How many chromosomes do humans have in most body cells?
questions.explanation: Human body cells have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 23 pairs make 46 chromosomes.

questions.question: Which body system is at work here? Your bones protect your brain.
questions.explanation: Your skull is bone protecting your brain, so it is the job of the skeletal system.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: link the action to the system.

questions.question: Which statement is part of cell theory?
questions.correctAnswer: All living things are made of cells
distractors: Cells are only found in animals
questions.explanation: Cell theory says all living things are made of cells, cells come from existing cells, and cells are the basic unit of life.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cells are the building blocks of all life.

questions.question: What is the function of the cell wall?
questions.correctAnswer: gives a plant cell shape and protection
distractors: breaks down waste and old cell parts
releases energy from food through cellular respiration
controls what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explanation: Made of cellulose, the cell wall is a rigid box around the cell that keeps its shape and blocks damage.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each organelle has one main job to remember.

questions.question: Which of these is a herbivore?
questions.explanation: A deer eats only plants, so it is a herbivore.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: herbivore means plant eater.

questions.question: Which of these is a main part of the immune system?
questions.explanation: White blood cells patrol the body and attack germs that do not belong there.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pair each system with its star organ.

questions.question: What is heredity?
questions.correctAnswer: passing traits from parents to offspring
distractors: a structure made of DNA that carries many genes
a characteristic that can be passed from parent to offspring
a section of DNA that codes for one trait
questions.explanation: heredity: passing traits from parents to offspring. (why children look like their parents)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genetics words build on each other, learn them in order.

questions.question: What is a consumer?
questions.correctAnswer: an organism that eats other organisms for energy
distractors: an organism that breaks down dead material
a relationship where one organism benefits and the other is not affected
many connected food chains in an ecosystem
questions.explanation: consumer: an organism that eats other organisms for energy. (a herbivore, carnivore, or omnivore)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: What is the main job of the circulatory system?
questions.correctAnswer: moves blood, oxygen, and nutrients around the body
distractors: sends signals and controls the body
supports the body and protects organs
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through vessels, delivering oxygen and nutrients to every cell and carrying waste away.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each body system has one big job.

questions.question: Which organelle is the jelly-like fluid where most cell activities happen?
questions.explanation: The cytoplasm is the jelly-like fluid that fills the cell; organelles float in it and most cell activities happen there.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: match the job to the worker.

questions.question: Which process releases energy from food in cells?
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration breaks down glucose with oxygen to release energy (ATP).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: respiration is how cells cash in their food for energy.

questions.question: Which organelle packages and ships proteins?
questions.explanation: The Golgi folds, labels, and ships proteins in vesicles to their destinations inside or outside the cell.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: match the job to the worker.

questions.question: What is the main job of the muscular system?
distractors: sends signals and controls the body
moves blood, oxygen, and nutrients around the body
brings oxygen into the body and removes carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Muscles pull on bones to move the body; they can only pull, never push, so they work in pairs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each body system has one big job.

questions.question: Which organ is a main part of the nervous system?
questions.explanation: The brain receives signals from the body, makes decisions, and sends orders back through the nerves.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pair each system with its star organ.

questions.question: Which gas do animals take in when they breathe?
questions.explanation: Animals breathe in oxygen, which cells use to release energy from food.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: oxygen is the fuel for cellular respiration.

questions.question: Which body system is at work here? You feel a hot stove and pull your hand away.
questions.explanation: Feeling the heat and pulling your hand away is the nervous system at work: it senses danger and sends the signal to move.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: link the action to the system.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of homeostasis?
questions.explanation: Sweating cools the body back toward its normal temperature.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sweating is your body turning on the air conditioning.

questions.question: What is a gene?
questions.correctAnswer: a section of DNA that codes for one trait
distractors: the molecule that carries genetic instructions
a structure made of DNA that carries many genes
questions.explanation: gene: a section of DNA that codes for one trait. (a unit of heredity)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genetics words build on each other, learn them in order.

questions.question: Which organ is a main part of the skeletal system?
questions.explanation: Bones are the key organs of the skeletal system: they support the body and protect organs like the brain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pair each system with its star organ.

questions.question: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen during photosynthesis.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plants breathe in what we breathe out.

questions.question: What is the main function of the root of a plant?
questions.correctAnswer: To absorb water and nutrients from the soil
questions.explanation: Roots take in water and minerals and anchor the plant.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: roots drink for the plant.

questions.question: Which organelle stores water and nutrients?
questions.explanation: The vacuole is a storage sac that holds water, nutrients, and waste until the cell needs them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: match the job to the worker.

questions.question: Which organ is a main part of the circulatory system?
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscle that squeezes about 100,000 times a day to push blood through the body.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pair each system with its star organ.

questions.question: In an experiment, what is the dependent variable?
questions.explanation: The dependent variable depends on the independent variable; it is what you measure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: dependent means it depends on what you changed.

questions.question: What is the function of the lysosome?
questions.correctAnswer: breaks down waste and old cell parts
distractors: releases energy from food through cellular respiration
the jelly-like fluid where most cell activities happen
questions.explanation: Lysosomes carry strong chemicals that digest worn-out cell parts and invaders, like a cleanup crew with dissolving soap.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each organelle has one main job to remember.

questions.question: What is a dominant trait?
questions.correctAnswer: a trait that shows up even if only one copy is inherited
distractors: a trait that shows up only if two copies are inherited
a chart that predicts the possible offspring of a cross
a change in the DNA sequence
questions.explanation: dominant trait: a trait that shows up even if only one copy is inherited. (shown by a capital letter in genetics)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: genetics words build on each other, learn them in order.

questions.question: Which organelle is a network of folded membranes where proteins are finished?
questions.explanation: The endoplasmic reticulum is a folded membrane network that finishes proteins and makes lipids.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the ER is the cell's workshop.

questions.question: What happens during mitosis?
questions.correctAnswer: One cell divides into two identical cells
distractors: One cell makes four different cells
A cell turns into a different type
questions.explanation: Mitosis is cell division that makes two identical copies for growth and repair.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: mitosis copies the cell exactly.

questions.question: Which cell part is found in both plant and animal cells?
questions.explanation: Both plant and animal cells have mitochondria to release energy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: both kinds of cells need power.

questions.question: What is the function of the ribosome?
distractors: releases energy from food through cellular respiration
controls the cell and holds the DNA
questions.explanation: Ribosomes float in the cytoplasm or sit on the endoplasmic reticulum, assembling proteins from amino-acid building blocks.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each organelle has one main job to remember.

questions.question: What is a mutualism?
questions.correctAnswer: a relationship where both organisms benefit
distractors: many connected food chains in an ecosystem
an organism that breaks down dead material
an animal that hunts other animals for food
questions.explanation: mutualism: a relationship where both organisms benefit. (like bees and flowers)
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ecology is about who eats whom and who helps whom.

questions.question: What is the function of the chloroplast?
distractors: releases energy from food through cellular respiration
controls what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explanation: Inside the chloroplast, chlorophyll captures sunlight to power the reaction that turns water and carbon dioxide into glucose.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each organelle has one main job to remember.

questions.question: Which is an example of an adaptation?
questions.correctAnswer: A polar bear has thick white fur
distractors: A bear lives in the Arctic
questions.explanation: Thick white fur helps the polar bear stay warm and hide in snow: that is an adaptation.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: adaptations are traits, not just behaviors or places.

questions.question: What is ATP in a cell?
questions.correctAnswer: The energy the cell uses to do work
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release energy from food and store it as ATP, the energy currency the cell spends to do work.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ATP is the cell's spendable energy.

questions.question: What holds a cell's shape and helps it move?
questions.explanation: The cytoskeleton is a network of tiny fibers that gives the cell its shape and helps it move and divide.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the cytoskeleton is the cell's skeleton.

questions.question: What is the job of white blood cells?
questions.explanation: White blood cells attack invaders like bacteria and viruses.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: white blood cells are the body's security team.

questions.question: What is the jelly-like substance inside a cell called?
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm fills the cell and holds the organelles in place.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cytoplasm is the cell's jelly.

questions.question: Which body system is at work here? Your lungs fill with air when you breathe in.
questions.explanation: Filling your lungs with air is the job of the respiratory system.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: link the action to the system.

questions.question: Which organ is a main part of the excretory system?
questions.explanation: The kidneys are the key organs of the excretory system: they filter waste out of the blood.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pair each system with its star organ.

questions.question: What is the main job of the excretory system?
distractors: supports the body and protects organs
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter waste from the blood, and the waste leaves the body as urine.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: each body system has one big job.

questions.question: Which process do cells use to take in water?
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water across a cell membrane.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: osmosis is water moving to balance things out.

questions.question: Which of these is a carnivore?
questions.explanation: A wolf eats meat, so it is a carnivore.

questions.question: What are the products of photosynthesis?
